q: Under the 2024 BP 344 IRR, a dropped sidewalk may sit at most how far above the road or gutter?
n: Under the 2024 BP 344 IRR, a dropped sidewalk (curb cut) may sit at most 19 mm above the road or gutter level. The older IRR allowed 25 mm. Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment).

q: At what height should door handles and lever locksets be for PWDs?
n: Door handles and lever locksets for PWDs are set at 0.90 m (900 mm) on centre from the floor. Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment), doors.

q: At what height is an accessible lavatory mounted?
n: An accessible lavatory is mounted with its rim at 0.80 m, with knee clearance of at least 650 mm beneath. Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment), toilets.

q: What is the minimum floor area of an accessible toilet cubicle?
n: An accessible toilet cubicle must be at least 1.80 × 1.80 m. Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment), accessible toilet cubicle.

q: Under the 2024 BP 344 IRR, what is the minimum clear width of a door?
n: The 2024 BP 344 IRR sets the minimum clear door width at 0.90 m, up from 0.80 m. Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment), doors.

q: A 1:20 ramp needs a landing every:
n: A 1:20 ramp needs a level landing every 15 m of run. Steeper 1:15 ramps need one every 10 m. Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment), ramp table.

q: What is the minimum clearance between a wall-mounted handrail and the wall?
n: Wall-mounted handrails need at least 50 mm clearance from the wall so hands can grip without scraping. Source: BP 344 IRR, Rule II, handrails.

q: What to put in a ramp sloping towards the street?
n: A ramp sloping toward the street needs railings (handrails and edge protection) so wheelchair users do not roll off into traffic. Source: BP 344 IRR, Rule II, ramps.

q: What is the seat height of an accessible water closet?
n: An accessible water closet seat is 0.45 m (450 mm) above the floor. Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment), toilets.

q: What clear walkway is needed between the front ends of parked cars in PWD parking?
n: PWD parking needs a clear walkway of at least 1.20 m between the front ends of parked cars. Source: BP 344 IRR, Rule II, parking.

q: According to BP344, what is the minimum width of a curb ramp?
n: A curb ramp must be at least 0.90 m wide for one wheelchair. Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment), curb ramps.

q: Under the 2024 BP 344 IRR, which turning space is too small?
n: The 2024 IRR minimum turning space is 1.80 × 1.80 m, so 1.50 m is now too small. Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment).

q: Under the 2024 BP 344 IRR, which accessible parking slot width is too narrow?
n: The 2024 IRR requires accessible parking slots of at least 4.00 × 5.00 m, so the old 3.70 m width is too narrow. Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment), parking.

q: What is the standard width of a wheelchair as stated under BP344?
n: The BP 344 IRR anthropometric figures give a standard wheelchair width of about 0.80 m, the basis for 0.90 m door and ramp widths. Source: BP 344 IRR, Annex (wheelchair dimensions).

q: Under BP 344, how far must handrails extend past the top and bottom of a ramp or stair?
n: Handrails must extend 0.30 m past the top and bottom of a ramp or stair. Source: BP 344 IRR, Rule II, handrails.

q: Under the 2024 BP 344 IRR, what is the minimum clear door opening of an accessible elevator?
n: Under the 2024 BP 344 IRR, an accessible elevator door needs a clear opening of at least 0.90 m (900 mm), so a wheelchair can enter straight on. Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment), elevators.

q: Under BP 344, walks should have ___ turn/groove in order to guide the blind?
n: Guide strips for blind users should change direction only at right angles. Walkways turn at 90° so cane users can follow the tactile groove or edge predictably. Source: BP 344 IRR, Rule II, walkways; ISO 23599 (tactile walking surface indicators).

q: What is the higher of the two handrail heights on accessible ramps and stairs?
n: Accessible ramps and stairs get dual handrails: the upper rail at 0.90 m and the lower at 0.70 m, for adults and wheelchair users or children. Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment), handrails.

q: What minimum vertical legroom should an accessible table or counter give?
n: Accessible tables and counters must leave at least 0.70 m of vertical knee and leg clearance beneath for wheelchair users. Source: BP 344 IRR, Rule II, counters and tables.

q: What is the preferred design for a stair considering users of crutches?
n: Crutch users catch their tips on projecting nosings and open risers. Stairs for them should have slanted (splayed) nosings flush with closed risers. Source: BP 344 IRR, Rule II, stairs; ICC A117.1 Sec. 504.5.

q: What is the maximum riser of an accessible stair?
n: Accessible stairs have risers of at most 150 mm and treads of at least 300 mm. Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment), stairs.

q: Under the 2024 BP 344 IRR, what is the minimum clear width of an accessible staircase?
n: The 2024 BP 344 IRR requires accessible staircases to have a clear width of at least 1.50 m. Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment), stairs.

q: What general conditions of design are important for the aged?
o: Height of lavatory is from the waist
n: Design for the aged must address all the listed points: fixture size, location and design, grab bars, and lavatory heights within easy reach. Source: BP 344 IRR, Rule II (elderly and PWD provisions).

q: What is the minimum depth of a central refuge?
n: A central refuge island must be at least 1.5 m deep (2.0 m preferred) so a wheelchair user can wait safely between traffic streams. Source: BP 344 IRR, Rule II, crossings.

q: What is the maximum lip height of an accessible urinal?
n: An accessible wall-hung urinal has its rim (lip) at most 0.40 m above the floor, typically 350–400 mm. Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment), toilets.

q: What clear space is needed in front of public telephones?
n: Public telephones for PWDs need a clear floor space of 1.80 × 1.80 m in front for wheelchair approach and turning. Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment), public telephones.

q: Under BP 344, what is the minimum width of a ramp?
n: Under BP 344, an accessible ramp must be at least 1.20 m clear between handrails. Source: BP 344 IRR, Rule II, ramps.

q: At most how high should telephone controls and coin slots be?
n: Telephone controls, dials and coin slots for PWDs should be no higher than 1.20 m above the floor. Source: BP 344 IRR, Rule II, telephones.

q: Wheelchair seating space for auditorium with 301-500 seating capacity?
n: BP 344 sets wheelchair spaces in assembly halls by seating capacity. For 301–500 seats it requires 6 spaces. Source: BP 344 IRR, Rule II, assembly seating table.

q: Air-conditioned buses shall have at least how many designated seats for disabled persons?
n: BP 344 requires first-class, premiere and air-conditioned buses to have at least four designated seats for disabled persons. Source: BP 344 IRR, Rule IV (public transportation).

q: Under the BP 344 IRR, what is the minimum clear distance of a handrail mounted on a ledge?
n: A handrail mounted on a ledge needs at least 40 mm clear distance so hands can grip it. Wall-mounted rails need 50 mm. Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment), handrails.

q: Ramps need handrails when the change in grade is higher than:
n: Ramps need handrails on both sides when the rise is more than 170 mm. Source: BP 344 IRR, Rule II, ramps.

q: What is the maximum threshold height?
n: Thresholds should be no higher than 12 mm. Those above 6 mm should be bevelled so wheelchairs can roll over them. Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment), doors and thresholds.

q: If thenewlywed wanted to add a space for a retail drugstore, what will you suggest as an architect?
o: Ask the newlywed not to put a retail drugstore because it is not good for aesthetic
Allow the retail drugstore but put in in the back side of the lot.
Retail, drugstores: are not allowed for residential duplexes since its purpose is for commercial
Put the retail drugstore accessible to the RROW
n: A retail drugstore is a commercial use, so it should be placed where it opens directly to and is accessible from the road right-of-way, separated from the private dwelling spaces and allowed by zoning. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII (mixed occupancy); HLURB/DHSUD Model Zoning Ordinance.
